Selected Ude.fetchHttp performs URL/log-target/timing preprocessing before its try, then prepares body/headers and calls performDesktopFetch with expectedIdentity/signal/progress/retry. It returns a Response wrapper for ok/304 or permitted returnErrorResponse, otherwise structured fetch-response errors. Only exceptions caught inside this try receive status499 for AbortError or500 otherwise unless the selected host error class supplies status; pre-try exceptions can propagate to provider cleanup/rethrow. Normal fetch can preserve an upstream response body, while performProgressRequest buffers data until end with Buffer.concat before constructing Response. No end-to-end streaming or runtime result is proven.

Selected performDesktopFetch applies network allow checks, explicit auth/surface/device/integrity destination guards, optional cached/loaded/refreshed auth and workspace routing/abort signals, conditional401 refresh, then applicationNetwork.fetch or progress request. These are source-confirmed controls; actual auth values, supplied applicationNetwork, imported token/header decoders, RPC base and successful network behavior remain unknown.

Provider destruction is wired to origin WebContents destroyed. Selected registerAppView awaits services on the remote view peer and uses clientCoordination/downloads; it is distinct from Zde.services on the host target. This matches the directional static upstream candidate and does not demonstrate live RPC delivery.

Selected Ue.fetch creates/maps an AbortController under request id, invokes the injected callback with id/request/signal/options, wraps response results through He and otherwise cleans up/returns unchanged; exceptions clean up/rethrow. He pipes a nonempty body with the signal and finally cleanup, or immediately cleans up an empty body. cancel aborts the currently mapped id; disposal aborts all mapped controllers and clears the Map. Id uniqueness, callback/stream completion and native APIs remain unverified.
